trips.title: Mojave Winter Loop
trips.subtitle: Death Valley, Joshua Tree, and the desert that only exists in January
trips.window: ⭐ Dec–Feb only. Every one of these is lethal or miserable May–September, which is exactly why they belong in the January window.
trips.region: Las Vegas → Death Valley → Mojave → Joshua Tree
trips.why:
🛑 Deferred, Sept 6 2026 — not happening in January 2027. His call, and it is not a scheduling problem: he would rather put the money into better places at better times of year than into the one window that happened to be free. Winter 2026–27 is Frisco with family and nothing else. The page is kept, not deleted — this is a Dec–Feb loop for whichever winter it lands in, and two verification passes are already done. The dates, the pin and the four booking rows are gone so the hub stops counting down to a trip nobody is taking; whenever it comes back, every one of those windows recomputes from new dates anyway.

⚠️ Rebuilding it later is not free. January 2027 was the only 19-day winter window before the horizon. After Aug 31 2027 a PTO allowance has to cover a 14-day loop plus travel, so the version that comes back will be a shorter one. That is the real cost of this decision and it is worth paying with open eyes.

Four low-elevation desert units inside one loop out of Las Vegas, all reachable on pavement, all in season only in winter: Valley of Fire (Aztec sandstone, ~1 hr from LAS), Death Valley (arguably the best-exposed geology in North America — Badwater, Zabriskie, Dante's View, Golden Canyon, Mesquite Dunes), Mojave National Preserve (Kelso Dunes, cinder cones, dispersed camping), and Joshua Tree.

⚠️ Racetrack Playa is out — it needs real clearance. ⚠️ Telescope Peak is 14 mi / ~3,000 ft, over the day ceiling. ⚠️ Every campground, fee and reservation rule here is unverified and must be checked before this becomes a page.

Routing is an open jaw off the family trip: CLE → DEN, Frisco Dec 25–30, DEN → LAS ~Jan 2, loop, LAS → CLE ~Jan 15. Ship a gear duffel to Las Vegas rather than hauling a tent and the MondoKing through a family Christmas; buy fuel canisters on arrival.
trips.next: Nothing. Deferred by choice — do not book anything. Revisit when a winter window turns up that is worth the airfare, and re-verify every campground rule from scratch when it does

trips.title: Eastern Sierra
trips.subtitle: Committed — the best payoff per dollar
trips.window: July–early October; September for aspen and fewer people
trips.why:
✅ Four Jeffrey CG at 8,100 ft with bear boxes and a trailhead under a mile up the road. Little Lakes Valley from Mosquito Flat is the highest paved trailhead in the Sierra — the single best expression of the car-camping rule set.

🔻 Confirmed Sept 6 2026 as the flex — the first of the three summer trips to drop. Not because it is the weakest; it is arguably the best value on the list. Because it is the only one that survives the horizon. Ten days on cheap Reno flights and a cheap car is a trip a two-week PTO allowance still holds in 2028 and every year after. Kenai and a three-week drive are not. Spending the last free summer on the one trip that keeps is the trade this whole plan exists to avoid.
trips.next: Hold the July slot but plan it last — if June and August both grow, this is what gets cut, and that is the correct outcome

trips.title: Beartooth Plateau
trips.subtitle: Paved to 9,500 ft
trips.window: Late June–early/mid September
trips.why:
📋 US-212 is paved above 9,500 ft, so you get emptiness and short approaches — everywhere else those two trade off. Island Lake CG sits at 9,518 ft. Pairs with Yellowstone's northeast corner for Lamar Valley wildlife with zero hiking.

🛑 The June 14 2027 target was removed Sept 6 2026, because it contradicted this entry's own window. "Late June–early/mid September" was already written here and a June 14 start is not late June. The verified detail is worse than the window suggests: ✅ US-212 opens around Memorial Day but does not stay open — in 2026 it opened May 23 and was closed again by snow at the Montana/Wyoming line, reopening June 9, then ran night closures 7 PM–7 AM Mon–Thu from Pilot Index east to Beartooth Lake. ✅ Beartooth Lake CG typically opens late June; sources on Island Lake disagree outright — one says late May, another says July 1 or earlier depending on snowpack — and a 9,518 ft campground is exactly where that disagreement is decided by the winter. Snow commonly lingers up high into early-to-mid July.

So a mid-June arrival buys a maybe-open road, probably-shut campgrounds and trails under snow. The plateau is a late-June-at-the-earliest trip and honestly a July one.

⚠️ `days` was 21 against `nights: ~7` in the same entry. The 21 was the road-trip container, not this trip. It is now 12 — seven nights on the plateau plus roughly 2.5 days of driving each way from Avon, which is ~1,700 mi. If a 21-day June road trip happens, this is one anchor inside it, not the whole thing.
trips.next: Do not target June again without calling Shoshone NF for Island Lake and Beartooth Lake opening dates — two published sources contradict each other by five weeks, and the answer decides whether the trip exists

trips.window: Mid-July–October, once the high road opens
trips.why: ✅ 29 paved miles topping out above 10,000 ft at Libby Flats, a 12,013 ft peak inside the day-hike ceiling, campgrounds above 10,000 ft, and no hiking permits of any kind. A fraction of Colorado's crowds two hours north of Denver.

trips.title: Kenai Peninsula
trips.subtitle: The one that gets harder to justify, not easier
trips.window: Late June for light, early September for color and fewer bugs
trips.budget: Highest on the list — flights and rentals triple a Reno rate
trips.why:
📋 Harding Icefield is the best single payoff on the entire bucket list. Four camps from Hatcher Pass to Exit Glacier, with a ~20% washout rate budgeted and the boat tour held back as a weather hedge.

⭐ Slotted for Aug 2027 — the last summer before full-time work. This is the trip the free summer exists for: every other fly-in on this list survives a two-week PTO allowance and this one does not. A PNW bundle (CLE→SEA→ANC→CLE) was considered and declined on purpose — Seattle is the natural connection so the routing was sound, but North Cascades is PTO-survivable and would have made Alaska the back half of a 24-day trip, and back halves get compressed.

✅ Rental cars: most Alaska companies prohibit unpaved roads outright and void insurance if you drive them — but the named restrictions (Denali Hwy, McCarthy, Steese, Dalton) are all interior. The Kenai's Seward and Sterling Highways are paved, so this is the least-affected corner of the state. ⚠️ Hatcher Pass is the exception and it is already in this plan — it sits north of Anchorage in the Mat-Su, not on the Kenai, and the summit traverse is gravel and seasonally gated. Paved approaches from either side are fine; the through-route is likely prohibited. Resolve before building the route.
trips.next: Get a named rental company's restricted-roads list in writing, and decide whether Hatcher Pass means the paved approach or the gravel traverse

trips.title: Capitol Reef
trips.subtitle: Maui return leg — the pick
trips.window: ⭐ May–Oct for hiking; early-to-mid May before the heat
trips.why:
The Waterpocket Fold is a 100-mile wrinkle in the Earth's crust — a monocline about as well exposed as any on the planet, and the entire reason the park exists. ✅ Least-visited of Utah's Mighty Five, so it passes the crowd test that Zion and Arches fail outright: no shuttle, no timed entry, no permit lottery.

✅ Fruita Campground — 71 sites in a historic orchard on the Fremont River, drive-up, reservable year-round on recreation.gov on a 6-month rolling window. The only established campground in the park, so book it.

Every hike fits the ceiling: Cassidy Arch (3.1 mi, ~850 ft), Chimney Rock, Grand Wash (flat, through the Fold itself), Hickman Bridge, Cohab Canyon. The Scenic Drive is paved; Cathedral Valley is the high-clearance half and you would simply skip it. ⚠️ Late May gets into the upper 80s — earlier in the month is better.
trips.next: Fruita books 6 months out and has 71 sites — that is the only real constraint here

trips.title: Dinosaur National Monument
trips.subtitle: Maui return leg — the sleeper
trips.window: Apr–Oct; May is ideal, before the summer heat
trips.budget: ✅ 191 mi, just over 3 hr from SLC — the shortest transfer of any option
trips.why:
The Quarry Exhibit Hall is a rock face with roughly 1,500 dinosaur bones still embedded in it — an in-situ Jurassic bone bed under a building, not a museum with casts. Then Split Mountain, where the Green River cuts straight through an anticline instead of going around it, which is the textbook example of an antecedent stream.

✅ Green River Campground: $12/night, open April–October with drinking water and flush toilets, on the riverbank under Split Mountain, five miles from the Quarry. ⚠️ Split Mountain Campground is group-only in peak season, so Green River is the one.

If the through-line is genuinely 'why does this landscape look like this', this is the most concentrated answer on the whole list — and almost nobody goes. Smaller than Capitol Reef, so three nights, not four.
trips.next: Confirm Green River Campground's April–October dates cover your week

trips.title: Black Canyon of the Gunnison
trips.subtitle: Colorado's one world-class May option
trips.window: ⚠️ Mid-May at the earliest — the South Rim road and campground are winter-closed until then
trips.budget: ~5 hr from DEN, ~1.5 hr from Montrose
trips.why:
Precambrian gneiss and schist, roughly 1.7–2 billion years old — the oldest rock you can stand next to in the region, and the Gunnison cut 2,000+ ft straight down into it. Narrow enough that parts of the floor get about half an hour of sun a day. The Painted Wall is Colorado's tallest cliff.

⚠️ Timing is razor-thin for a mid-May return. In 2026 the South Rim Campground opened May 18, and Loops B and C were closed by wildfire damage, leaving Loop A only. The South Rim Road is winter-closed and reopens in May. East Portal opens Apr 15 but sits at the bottom of a 16% grade; North Rim opens May 1 with 13 sites down a remote gravel road.

⚠️ It is a rim park — you look into it rather than walk it. The inner-canyon routes are unmaintained, brutally steep and permit-required, so the hiking is short rim trails. Two nights, not four.
trips.next: Check whether the South Rim opening date and the wildfire loop closures still apply before counting on it

trips.title: Colorado National Monument
trips.subtitle: The reliable Colorado option in May
trips.window: Mar–Oct; May is warm and snow-free
trips.budget: ~4 hr from DEN, 20 min from Grand Junction
trips.why:
Sheer red rock canyons and monoliths off Rim Rock Drive, at 4,700–6,600 ft — low enough to be snow-free in May when the Colorado mountains are still unusable. Monument Canyon, Window Rock, Canyon Rim and the Alcove Nature Trail all leave from near the visitor center.

✅ Saddlehorn Campground: 79 sites, March–October, $22, reservable on recreation.gov, four miles from the Fruita entrance. Loop C is tents and small campers only — that is the one to want. The only established campground in the monument.

Pairs naturally with Black Canyon, 2.5 hours away, for a Western Slope loop out of Grand Junction.
trips.next: Book Loop C at Saddlehorn if this becomes the plan

trips.title: Great Sand Dunes
trips.subtitle: Maui return leg — with a real catch
trips.window: Late May–June for Medano Creek — but see the warning
trips.why:
Tallest dunes in North America — 750 ft of sand piled against the Sangre de Cristos. Your bucket list flags late May for Medano Creek: sand plus water, a completely different kind of day.

🛑 Do not build a trip around the creek. 2026 is no longer a forecast — it is a result. This entry previously said the creek "likely would not flow at all"; it didn't. ✅ Peak flow came in around 4 cfs against a 40 cfs average, the NPS called watershed snowpack near record low, and by May 21 2026 the creek was dry at the main Dunes Parking Area, petering out roughly 1.5 miles up the creekbed. Anyone who booked late May 2026 for surge flow got sand.

So the creek is a coin flip decided in March, and it is the only thing that makes this a June destination rather than a two-hour stop. 2027 is unknowable until that winter happens. Be content with just dunes, or do not come for the water.

✅ Piñon Flats: 88 sites, $20, reservable 6 months out, drive-up.
trips.next: Check Sangre de Cristo snowpack in March 2027 before this becomes a plan — and note that the 6-month booking window for a late-May trip closes before you would know the answer

trips.title: Owens Valley + Alabama Hills
trips.subtitle: Maui bookend — the outbound leg
trips.window: ⭐ Apr–May and Oct — too hot in summer, snowbound above
trips.budget: 3.5 hr drive from LAX or Burbank
trips.why: The Sierra escarpment is about 10,000 ft of relief in a few horizontal miles — one of the great normal-fault fronts on Earth — and the 1872 Lone Pine earthquake scarp is walkable at the valley floor. Weathered granite at Alabama Hills, basalt scoured by the Owens River at Fossil Falls, and Manzanar for the ruins. This is also the only piece of the Eastern Sierra that works in May, so it doubles as a scouting trip for the committed summer version. ⚠️ Alabama Hills is now designated sites only (~50, first-come) plus a free one-year permit; no camping west of Movie Road. Tuttle Creek BLM — already on your Eastern Sierra list as the bad-weather fallback — is the drive-up base.
trips.next: Get the free Alabama Hills permit online, and check whether AAA waives the young-renter fee on a second and third rental

trips.title: Point Reyes + Marin
trips.subtitle: The Maui return leg
trips.window: Apr–Jun — spring wildflowers, before the summer fog wall thickens
trips.why:
The San Andreas runs straight through it — the Earthquake Trail has a fence line offset about 20 feet by the 1906 rupture, and the whole peninsula is a slab of granite rafted roughly 300 miles north from the southern Sierra. Tule elk at Tomales Point (~9.4 mi, nearly flat), Bear Valley out to Arch Rock, Chimney Rock. Maximally unlike Maui — cold fog, dairy ranches and a transform fault, three days after a shield volcano.

⚠️ NPS is explicit: there is no car camping inside the Seashore. All four in-park campgrounds are hike-in. The base is Samuel P. Taylor SP — 60 developed plus 16 tent-only sites in redwoods on Lagunitas Creek, reservable through ReserveCalifornia, about 35 min from Bear Valley. Treat it as a redwood basecamp with coastal day trips rather than a compromise.

⚠️ May fog and wind are the real risk — the outer point is one of the windiest, foggiest places on the Pacific coast. Keep Chimney Rock and the lighthouse flexible; Bear Valley, Olema Valley and Samuel P. Taylor stay clear when the point is socked in. ✅ Elk: fence removal began Dec 2024 but most of the herd still holds the Tomales Point reserve, so the viewing stands.

Food: Point Reyes Station — Cowgirl Creamery, Bovine Bakery, and Tomales Bay oysters as the regional dish.
trips.next: Check Samuel P. Taylor May availability — ReserveCalifornia, 6 months out

trips.title: Pinnacles
trips.subtitle: A volcano the San Andreas tore in half
trips.window: Mar–May and Oct — summer is brutal
trips.why: ⚠️ A 23-million-year-old volcanic field split by the San Andreas and carried 195 miles north from where it erupted — the other half is still down at Neenach. Talus caves, rhyolite spires, condors. ⚠️ Two real problems for May: over 80% of annual visitation happens in spring with long queues 10 AM–3 PM, and Bear Gulch Cave closes mid-May to mid-July for bat pupping. Midweek only, and check which caves are open.
trips.next: Only if you can go midweek — otherwise it fails the crowd test outright

trips.title: Sequoia + Kings Canyon
trips.subtitle: The big-tree bookend
trips.window: May works low; Mineral King road opens late May
trips.budget: ~4 hr from LAX, ~1.5 hr from Fresno
trips.why: ⚠️ Giant Forest and Grant Grove are reachable in May when the high country is not. The largest trees on Earth by volume, plus glaciated granite. ⚠️ Mineral King — the quiet corner — is a narrow 25-mile road that usually opens late May, so an early-May trip gets the busy half of the park. Fits the outbound leg from LAX better than the return.
trips.next: Check the Mineral King road opening date against your dates before choosing this over Owens Valley

trips.title: Buffalo National River
trips.subtitle: The penciled 2027 shoulder trip
trips.window: Apr–May and Oct — April is waterfalls, summer is swimming
trips.why: ✅ The only dam-free river of its kind and the best warm swimming on the whole list. April is peak waterfall and wildflower season and the upper river is only navigable in spring. Hemmed-In Hollow is the tallest waterfall between the Rockies and the Appalachians; Whitaker Point, Big Bluff and Lost Valley all day-hike from a drive-up base. ⚠️ Kyles Landing fails the clearance test — 3 miles of very steep gravel, 4WD recommended. Steel Creek is the base: 26 tent-only sites under Roark Bluff, water and flush restrooms roughly Mar 15–Nov 15.
trips.next: Reservations required since Mar 2026 at Steel Creek and four others — 6-month window, so an early-April 2027 trip books around early October 2026

trips.title: Sipsey Wilderness
trips.subtitle: Land of a Thousand Waterfalls
trips.window: ⭐ Feb–April for water — but the drive-up bases do not open until March. See below.
trips.why:
⚠️ The largest designated wilderness east of the Mississippi, with dozens of waterfalls, sandstone box canyons, huge old growth and swimming holes. The one place on the whole list whose peak window is early spring specifically — its waterfalls only run with the water. Day-hike into the wilderness from a drive-up base rather than backpacking it.

✅ Corrected Sept 2026 — the earlier "open April–October" note here was wrong. Clear Creek opens the second Friday of March and closes Oct 31; reservation-only via recreation.gov. Corinth ran Mar 8–Oct 31 in 2026, part reservable and part first-come. So the season starts in early-to-mid March, not April — but a trip starting in the first week of March has no open established campground in Bankhead.
trips.next: Second Friday of March 2027 is the 12th — a Mar 5–15 window only catches Clear Creek for three nights. Confirm Corinth's 2027 opening date by phone (205-300-1463) before this becomes an early-March plan.

trips.title: Grand Staircase–Escalante
trips.subtitle: Warm desert water, which barely exists out west
trips.window: Apr–May and Oct
trips.why: ⚠️ Lower Calf Creek, the Zebra and Tunnel slots, Devil's Garden and Willis Creek all still work as day hikes. Warm swimmable desert water is genuinely rare out west, where most water is 37–50°F. ⚠️ The centrepiece — Coyote Gulch via Hurricane Wash — is out under the no-backpacking rule, so this is a lesser version of the trip that was researched.
trips.next: Decide whether the day-hike version is still worth a plane ticket

trips.title: Sky Islands
trips.subtitle: Spring break — the strangest biology in the US, and one eruption weathered three ways
trips.window: Nov–Apr — ⭐ Feb, March and April are the good months, and they are also the full ones
trips.why:
⚠️ Heart of Rocks and Echo Canyon are the marquee day hikes through rhyolite hoodoo forests — welded ash from the Turkey Creek caldera, so the geology is the whole point rather than a footnote. The Dragoons are the counterpoint at 1.4 billion years, and you can see one range from the other.

✅ Verified Sept 2026 — the facts that decide whether March works: Chiricahua charges no entrance fee. Bonita Canyon (~5,400 ft) is year-round, 23–26 sites, all reservable, no walk-ups, 6-month rolling window, full most nights in its Feb–April peak. Sunny Flat is year-round first-come — but potable water is off until April, and Cochise Stronghold has none at any time of year: four of ten nights are haul-your-own. 🚨 Rustler Park and FR 42D are closed Nov–March and unplowed, so the eight miles between the monument and Portal cost 2h 35m around on I-10, and the high country is off the trip.

⚠️ Turn your own rule on this before booking it. "Actively avoids crowds" is the profile, and March is the monument's busiest month; a reservation removes the lottery, not the people. The itinerary answers that with a split — 3 nights in the monument, 7 outside it — and puts the two hardest days on a Wednesday and a Saturday.
trips.next: Bonita Canyon is 23–26 sites on a 6-month rolling window and there is no walk-up fallback inside the monument — Mar 8 released around Sept 8 2026 and each later night releases one day at a time. Then price CLE → TUS, which is the only number on the page that could swing $400

booking.note: All sites reservable, no first-come option, full most nights Feb–April. If this fails, the middle of the trip fails.

trips.title: Wichita Mountains
trips.subtitle: Free-roaming bison and granite domes
trips.window: Nov–Apr
trips.budget: Drive, ~14 hrs — or fly to OKC
trips.why: ⚠️ Doris CG, free-roaming bison, granite domes, Elk Mountain and Charons Garden. Almost nobody outside Oklahoma has heard of it. Small enough to pair with something rather than carry a trip alone.
trips.next: Probably a pairing, not a destination — decide what it pairs with

trips.title: Great Smokies — the east side
trips.subtitle: Where it stops being a traffic jam
trips.window: Late Apr–May, and Oct
trips.why: ⚠️ Cataloochee, Big Creek, Balsam Mountain and Deep Creek — the east side is the crowd escape. Mount Cammerer and Ramsey Cascades are the day hikes; Gregory Bald is a June thing. ⚠️ Late April, not early — the higher country and some roads are still shut at the start of the month.
trips.next: Only worth it after ~April 20 — check road and campground opening dates

trips.title: South Cumberland + Fall Creek Falls
trips.subtitle: The Plateau's real gems
trips.window: Apr–May and Oct–Nov
trips.why: ⚠️ Foster Falls, Savage Gulf and the Stone Door, plus Fall Creek Falls SP. Same Cumberland Plateau geology as the Sept 2026 Big South Fork trip but a completely separate area — worth knowing you will have just seen this rock type six months earlier.
trips.next: Decide whether it is too soon after Big South Fork

trips.title: Ohiopyle
trips.subtitle: Best swimming per mile driven on the whole list
trips.window: Late spring through early autumn — April is cold for the slides
trips.why: ⚠️ Meadow Run natural waterslides — actual sliding on rock, not a novelty plunge. Ferncliff Peninsula, Baughman Rock, the Youghiogheny. Kentuck Campground. Ranked #2 on the swimming list and it is three and a half hours from your door.
trips.next: The obvious cheap counterweight to an expensive year — but the water is cold before May

trips.title: Letchworth
trips.subtitle: Four hours away and never once mentioned
trips.window: Apr–Oct; spring for waterfall volume
trips.why: ⚠️ The Grand Canyon of the East — three major waterfalls, 600 ft gorge walls, drive-up camping. Spring is when the falls actually have volume. Four hours from your door and it has never come up once in your planning history.
trips.next: A two-night April shakedown that costs a tank of gas

trips.title: Newfoundland
trips.subtitle: The Earth's mantle, a Viking hall, and icebergs — the June trip that actually is a June trip
trips.window: June–September. ⭐ June is genuinely peak here rather than a compromise — icebergs, 17-hour days, no heat.
trips.budget: Ferry ~$350–400 USD round trip; no airfare at all
trips.why:
⭐ The single best geology destination on this list, and it is not close. The Tablelands at Gros Morne is exposed oceanic mantle — peridotite obducted onto the continent — and it is the reason the park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site: it is the physical evidence that confirmed plate tectonics. ✅ AllTrails: 4.9 mi, 705 ft, Moderate, and open all of June. Everything else on the geology-as-through-line list is rock; this is the layer underneath the rock.

✅ L'Anse aux Meadows opens June 1. North America's only confirmed Norse settlement, c. 1000 AD. "Ruins count as scenery" has no better answer anywhere on the continent.

✅ Icebergs peak late May–early June and are present to early July — Twillingate, Bonavista, St. Anthony. Icebergs and whales on the same boat is routine in that window. ✅ Mid-June daylight at Gros Morne runs first light 4:30 AM to dark 10:13 PM — about 17 usable hours, computed. That is most of the "late June for light" argument that justifies Kenai, for a tenth of the money.

🚨 The trip does not fit in 21 days and Newfoundland + the Maritimes does not fit at all. Cleveland → Nova Scotia is ~1,250–1,290 mi and ~23 hrs, and North Sydney is further out Cape Breton — call it 3 days each way at the +15% rule. Six of 21 days are transit before the ferry. Pick Newfoundland or pick the Maritimes; both is a fantasy.

✅ The routing that fixes it: ferry North Sydney → Argentia (14–16 hrs, lands near St. John's), drive the island east to west, ferry home from Port aux Basques (7 hrs). No road driven twice, and it saves ~900 km of backtracking. ⚠️ Argentia is seasonal — June 19 to Sept 30 in 2026 (Mon/Thu/Sat, 5:30 PM), so this routing does not exist before about June 19. Verify the 2027 dates.

⚠️ Three dates fight each other: peak icebergs (late May–early June), the Argentia ferry (June 19+), and the Gros Morne Mountain summit (closed May 1–June 27 for caribou calving). You cannot have the first two together. The summit is the cheapest thing to lose — AllTrails puts it at 10.8 mi / 3,044 ft, which is over the day ceiling on both counts, and it is the crowded one. Tablelands, Green Gardens (6.6 mi / 1,266 ft) and the Tablelands Off-Trail Loop (7.4 mi / 1,925 ft) are all open in June and all fit inside the ceiling.

⚠️ It is cold and wet, not cool and pleasant. Rocky Harbour June normals are 40–44°F low / 64–68°F high, but 2026 actuals ran highs of 49–67°F, consistently under normal, with coastal fog. The Siesta 20 is the right bag; the failure mode is twelve days of rain, not one cold night. ✅ Blackflies exist but coastal wind holds them down — Gros Morne is reported as usually fine, unlike the Lake Superior option this replaced.

⚠️ Needs a valid passport, which is a months-long lead time if there isn't one. ⚠️ Ferry: roughly $60/adult + $120–180 vehicle one-way plus a 13% fuel surcharge, after the federal rate cut of Aug 2025 — call it $350–400 USD round trip, and note that a rate cut is a policy that can lapse before 2027. ⚠️ The Western Brook Pond boat ($99 in 2026) needs 15 people to run, which is a real risk for a solo traveller in shoulder-season June.

⭐ Passes the horizon test better than anything else on the list. A 26-day drive from Ohio to Newfoundland is precisely what a two-week PTO allowance can never hold. You can fly to Deer Lake later; you cannot do this later.
trips.next: Decide the trade first — Newfoundland or the Maritimes, and peak icebergs or the Argentia no-backtrack routing. Then check whether a valid passport exists, because that has the longest lead time of anything here

trips.title: Bighorns / Cloud Peak
trips.subtitle: Unspent and cheap to reach
trips.window: Mid-June–September — earlier than the rest of the alpine tier, which is the point
trips.why:
📋 Crazy Woman Canyon Road dispersed camping — creek, canyon walls, the best-reviewed sites in the range. Cut from the overlanding trip and never reallocated.

✅ Corrected Sept 6 2026 — this was filed as July–September and that was wrong. Several Cloud Peak Skyway (US-16) campgrounds open June 5, which makes the Bighorns the one entry in the alpine tier that is genuinely in season in June. ⚠️ The caveat is elevation-dependent: high-country roads in the range can stay snow-packed until about July 1, so the Skyway corridor works in mid-June and the highest side roads may not. That distinction is exactly what a Beartooth trip does not get — US-212 is above 9,500 ft for its whole length, so there is no low half of it to fall back on.
trips.next: The Calendar could not offer this for a June window until now. If a June road trip happens, this is the alpine anchor that actually works that month — verify Crazy Woman Canyon Rd against 5.9 in of clearance first
